name: Babylonia
alt: Dynasty IV of Babylon (Second Dynasty of Isin)

predecessors.name: Akkadian Empire
predecessors.text: a tract of land around Babylon appropriated by Sumu-abum

successors.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
successors.text: Babylonia restored as an independent kingdom by Nabopolassar

ledger.x: 1894 BC: Sumu-abum founds Babylon's First Dynasty.
c. 1764 BC: Hammurabi turns on Larsa. "Around 1764 BC, Hammurabi turned against Rim-Sin, who had refused to support Hammurabi in his war against Elam despite pledging his troops." Mirrors larsa.

c. 1763 BC: the siege ends. "Hammurabi's forces quickly reached Larsa, and after a six-month siege the city fell." The page dates Rim-Sin's death "c. 1763 BC"; the annexation follows in the next event. Mirrors larsa.
c. 1763 BC: Hammurabi annexes Larsa and the whole lower plain. "Hammurabi invaded and then annexed Larsa, thus gaining control of the entirety of the lower Mesopotamian plain around 1763 BC."
1762 BC (Hammurabi year 31): Babylon occupies Eshnunna.

c. 1761 BC: Babylon ends the Lim dynasty of Mari. "Babylon invaded in c. 1761 BC under the rule of Hammurabi and defeated Zimri-Lin, ending the Lim dynasty"; Terqa then "became the capital of the rump Kingdom of Hana" and "the Suhum region became a Babylonian province". The Hammurabi page: "conquered the remaining…

c. 1751 BC: Assyria pays tribute. Hammurabi "forced their successor Mut-Ashkur to pay tribute to Babylon c. 1751 BC"; the Old Assyrian period page adds that Hammurabi "appears to have respected Assur and its institutions".

c. 1732-1721 BC: Sumer secedes under Ilum-ma-ili. "A few years later, a pretender calling himself Ilum-ma-ili" raised "another pan-Sumerian revolt", dated "between the 18th and 29th year of Samsu-iluna's reign" (accession 1749, middle chronology: 1732-1721); he "founded the First Dynasty of Sea-Land". The Rim-Sin II…

By the end of Samsu-iluna's reign (1712) Assyria is free: Puzur-Sin "ejected Asinum", Adasi "restored a stable native dynasty" removing "any vestages of Amorite-Babylonian influence"; the page gives no year and says Samsu-iluna "seems to have been powerless to intervene".
Cliopatria's -1700 shape no longer reaches the Euphrates or Mari (west edge 43.4 E).
1595 BC: the Hittites sack Babylon and the Kassites take the throne.

c. 1460 BC: the Kassites absorb the Sealand and Sumer. "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC created a power vacuum which the Kassites filled"; the Babylonia page dates Ulamburiash's attack "around 1450 BC" and the Sealand page ends the dynasty c. 1475.
Cliopatria widens the shape at -1400 to 226,484 km2 (north to 35.6 N, west to 40 E, south to Kuwait).
Mid 14th century BC: Kurigalzu I invades Elam.
The page gives no duration; the occupation of Elam is closed one year after it began.
1155 BC: Shutruk-Nakhunte ends the Kassite dynasty.
Babylonia returns under the Second Dynasty of Isin.
Babylonia shrinks to its core in Cliopatria's -1000 shape.
Cliopatria regrows the shape in -900 to 118,948 km2.
729 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon.
721-710 BC: Marduk-apla-iddina holds Babylon.
710 BC: Sargon II retakes Babylon.

Babylon has a king of its own again by 652 (Shamash-shum-ukin revolts "in 652 BCE"); the pages give no date for the end of direct Assyrian rule or for Sennacherib's and Esarhaddon's arrangements ("Babylon was destroyed" in 689).
652 BC: Shamash-shum-ukin revolts at Babylon.
648 BC: Ashurbanipal takes Babylon.

Nov. 626 BC: Nabopolassar founds the Chaldean (Neo-Babylonian) dynasty. "Nabopolassar was formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE, restoring Babylonia as an independent kingdom." Same state, new dynasty; the neo-babylonian-empire dossier continues the land.

wars.name: Hammurabi's conquest of Larsa
wars.outcome: Hammurabi annexed Larsa around 1763 and gained "the entirety of the lower Mesopotamian plain"; Rim-Sin I was Hammurabi's earlier ally.

wars.name: Hammurabi's northern campaigns
wars.outcome: "Soon after" Larsa he destroyed Eshnunna and his armies took the northern states including Mari (possibly a surrender); Mut-Ashkur of Assyria paid tribute c.

wars.name: Revolt of Rim-Sin II
wars.outcome: In the ninth year of Samsu-iluna a man calling himself Rim-Sin raised a revolt that "spread to include some 26 cities"; he was killed when "Larsa itself was defeated".

wars.name: Ilum-ma-ili's revolt and the First Sealand dynasty
wars.outcome: Ilum-ma-ili's pan-Sumerian revolt "founded the First Dynasty of Sea-Land"; by Samsu-iluna's death "Nippur recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king".

wars.name: Hittite sack of Babylon
wars.outcome: "Babylon was then attacked by the Indo-European-speaking, Anatolia-based Hittites in 1595 BC"; no land passed to Hatti.

wars.name: Kassite conquest of the Sealand
wars.outcome: Ulam-Buriash "conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia"; Agum III attacked it again, destroying a temple in Dur-Enlil.

wars.name: Assyrian intervention under Ashur-uballit I
wars.outcome: "in 1333 BC, a usurper named Nazi-Bugaš deposed him [Kara-hardash], enraging Ashur-uballit I, who invaded and sacked Babylon"; Kurigalzu II was placed on the Kassite throne.

wars.name: Kurigalzu II and Enlil-nirari at Sugagi
wars.outcome: The Synchronistic Chronicle: the kings "divided the districts from Šasili of Subartu, to Karduniaš into two and fixed the boundary-line"; the epic texts "may perhaps suggest an indecisive outcome".

wars.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I's conquest of Babylonia
wars.outcome: "the Assyrian king Tukulti-Ninurta I (1243-1207 BC) routed his armies, sacked and burned Babylon"; Kashtiliash IV was deposed c.

wars.name: Elamite conquest of Babylonia
wars.outcome: Shutruk-Nakhunte conquered Babylon and carried off the Statue of Marduk; the Kassite dynasty ended.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar I's war with Elam
wars.outcome: Nebuchadnezzar I "routed the Elamite king Ḫulteludiš-Inšušinak on the banks of the river Ulaya" and recovered the statue of Marduk in a surprise summer attack from Der; "No contemporary or later source records a sack of Susa".

wars.name: Shalmaneser III in Babylonia
wars.outcome: Shalmaneser III, "in 851-850 BCE, aided the Babylonian king Marduk-zakir-shumi I to defeat a revolt by his brother"; the Babylonia page says he "sacked Babylon itself" (859-824).

wars.name: Shamshi-Adad V against Marduk-balassu-iqbi
wars.outcome: "In 813 BCE, he defeated Marduk-balassu-iqbi and brought him to Assyria as a captive."

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's conquest of Babylon
wars.outcome: "In 729 BCE, he captured Babylon, defeated Nabu-mukin-zēri"; he ruled Babylon directly.

wars.name: Sargon II's Babylonian campaign
wars.outcome: Sargon "encountered little resistance" in 710 and displaced Marduk-apla-iddina.

wars.name: Revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin
wars.outcome: Shamash-shum-ukin revolted in 652 with Elamite help; Ashurbanipal captured Babylon after a long siege in 648.

certainty.note: Last year of the state; the Neo-Babylonian Empire continues it.
